title: Deep Learning Improves Pancreatic Cancer Diagnosis Using RNA-Based Variants
summary: Deep-learning analysis of RNA-sequencing-derived variants distinguished resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma from chronic pancreatitis in a held-out cohort. Combining variant features with CA19-9 yielded a test AUC of 0.96, compared with 0.89 for variant features alone. This does not establish screening performance or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Deep-learning models analyze RNA-based variant features alongside CA19-9 for pancreatic-cancer classification.
organization: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center; University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The study included 268 participants: 87 with resectable pancreatic cancer, 96 with non-resectable cancer and 85 with chronic pancreatitis. The reported combined-model test AUC for resectable cancer versus pancreatitis was 0.96.
evidence.unknown: Single-study dataset evaluation with no external prospective validation; does not establish population screening utility.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning models analyze RNA-based variant features alongside CA19-9 for pancreatic-cancer classification.
